sentences.text: These fish possessed small plates covering their heads and rod-shaped scales arranged in a chevron pattern on their trunks.
The genus Birkenia was formally described by Traquair in 1898.
Intact fossils of B. elegans indicate the animal grew up to 10.0 cm long and was an active swimmer.
Fossil evidence shows a modified rib structure that is narrow at the ends and broadens toward the middle to form a raised, slightly angled ridge.
Birkenia is classified within the class Anaspida and belongs to the family Birkeniidae.
Three species are known within the genus: B. campbelli, B. elegans, and B. robusta.
Birkenia existed between 443.1 and 422.7 million years ago during the Rhuddanian to Ludfordian stages.
It lived during the Middle Silurian in Northern Europe and possibly the Earliest Devonian in Arctic Canada.
